title: Lemma 2.5 (AFP): (eq:tree) uses wrong conjugation form; orthogonality fails as written (breaks Case B)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** `solution.tex`, Lemma `lem:afp` (AFP step), equation (eq:tree), first inequality, and its in-text justification.

**Statement as written.**
$$u_1^*\,\lambda_1(e_B)\,u_1+u_2^*\,\lambda_1(e_B)\,u_2\ \le\ \lambda_2(e_B),\qquad u_3^*\,\lambda_2(e_B)\,u_3\le\lambda_1(e_B).$$

**Gap / error.** The first inequality is a *sum of two projections*; for it to be dominated by the projection $\lambda_2(e_B)$ the two summand-ranges must be **orthogonal**. With the displayed conjugation-by-$u_j^{*}$ form the relevant ranges are $u_1^{*}(\operatorname{ran}\lambda_1(e_B))$ and $u_2^{*}(\operatorname{ran}\lambda_1(e_B))$, and a direct reduced-word computation gives
$$\langle u_1^{*}\xi,\,u_2^{*}\eta\rangle=\langle u_2u_1^{*}\xi,\eta\rangle,\qquad \xi,\eta\in\operatorname{ran}\lambda_1(e_B),$$
whose only possibly-nonzero contribution is the $B$-part $E_B(u_2u_1^{*})$. So orthogonality with the $u_j^{*}$ form requires $E_B(u_2u_1^{*})=0$. But the **stated hypothesis** of the lemma is $E_B(u_1^{*}u_2)=0$ (equivalently $E_B(u_2^{*}u_1)=0$), which instead justifies orthogonality for the conjugation-by-$u_j$ form $u_j\,\lambda_1(e_B)\,u_j^{*}$. Indeed the in-text justification itself writes "$u_1\eta\perp u_2\eta'$" — the $u_j$ form — **contradicting** the displayed inequality.

**Why this is consequential (not cosmetic).** In the application (Theorem `thm:main`, **Case B**, $|W|=1$) one takes $u_1=a_w$, $u_2=b\,a_w$ with $b\in M_{u'}\subseteq B$. Then
$$E_B(u_2u_1^{*})=E_B(b\,a_w a_w^{*})=b\neq0,\qquad\text{while}\qquad E_B(u_1^{*}u_2)=E_B(a_w^{*}b\,a_w)=0.$$
So the displayed (eq:tree) orthogonality genuinely **fails in Case B**, whereas the correct $u_j\,\lambda_1(e_B)\,u_j^{*}$ form succeeds. As written the lemma is therefore incorrect and internally inconsistent.

**Suggested fix.** Replace the first inequality by
$$u_1\,\lambda_1(e_B)\,u_1^{*}+u_2\,\lambda_1(e_B)\,u_2^{*}\ \le\ \lambda_2(e_B),$$
and prove: (a) $u_j(\operatorname{ran}\lambda_1)\subseteq\operatorname{ran}\lambda_2$ (prepending the $M_1^o$-letter $u_j$ to a word beginning in $M_2^o$ or $B$ yields a word beginning in $M_1^o$); (b) orthogonality $u_1(\operatorname{ran}\lambda_1)\perp u_2(\operatorname{ran}\lambda_1)$ from $E_B(u_2^{*}u_1)=E_B(u_1^{*}u_2)^{*}=0$. Since $\varphi$ is conjugation-invariant the numerical evaluation $2a\le b\le a$, $a+b=1$ is unchanged. (The second inequality has no sum and is fine in either form.)

comments.body:
## Critic re-confirmation against current `solution.tex` — STILL A LIVE ERROR

`eq:tree` in the current `solution.tex` is still displayed in the $u_j^*$-conjugation form
$$u_1^*\lambda_1(e_B)u_1+u_2^*\lambda_1(e_B)u_2\le\lambda_2(e_B),$$
while the in-text justification proves the $u_j$-form ("$u_1\xi$ begins in $M_1^o$ ... $u_1\eta\perp u_2\eta'$"). Orthogonality of the two summand ranges in the displayed form needs $E_B(u_2u_1^*)=0$ ⇔ $E_B(u_1u_2^*)=0$, NOT the hypothesis $E_B(u_1^*u_2)=0$. Verified to fail in main-theorem Case B: $u_1=a_w$, $u_2=ba_w$ ($b\in B$) give $u_1u_2^*=a_wa_w^*b^*=b^*\in B$, so $E_B(u_1u_2^*)=b^*\neq0$ and the displayed inequality is false. **Fix:** display the $u_j$-form $u_1\lambda_1u_1^*+u_2\lambda_1u_2^*\le\lambda_2$; the trace step $2a\le b$ is unaffected by $M$-centrality.
